newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan shows interest in issuing samurai bonds.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan shows interest in issuing samurai bonds.

text.p: Pakistan is to hold a road show in Tokyo later this week and will investigate the possibility of issuing a samurai bond, a senior government official said on Monday.

Shahid Javed Burki, finance and economic affairs adviser to the caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid told a news conference that he would go to Tokyo on Wednesday to make presentations in the Japanese market.
"Our view is that the yen market is a good market to raise money and I have been invited by the Japanese to make some presentations, a kind of road show in Tokyo," he said.
Asked if Pakistan will issue a samurai bond, he said "We are certainly looking into the possibility of a samurai bond." But he gave no details.

Burki said he was going to Japan to earn Tokyo's support for a programme the caretaker government has undertaken for economic revival after the dismissal of prime minister Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5.

"We also want to re-establish good working relationship on economic issues with the government of Japan," he said. "The government of Japan had not been very happy with the way we had been implementing their projects in the past."
